capture_source:
#!/bin/bash
wump_evidence=/home/marcus/projects/wump/master/build/checkpoint-xs-json
wump_stock=/home/marcus/projects/wump/master/build/checkpoint-7a16547/stock/perl/perl-5.42.2/perl
wump_go=/home/marcus/projects/wump/master/build/checkpoint-runtime-owner/integration/matrix-go
wump_after="$wump_evidence/final/perl/perl-5.42.2/perl"
export LC_ALL=C LANG=C TZ=UTC
if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then printf '%s\n' 'Refusing timing capture with dirty sources.' >&2; exit 1; fi
if ! taskset -c 0,2,4,6 perl bench/matrix.pl "$wump_after" "$wump_stock" "$wump_go" --runs 5 --iterations 50000 --jobs 8 --output "$wump_evidence/matrix-current.json" > "$wump_evidence/matrix-current.md" 2> "$wump_evidence/matrix-current.stderr"; then
 printf '%s\n' 'Matrix capture failed.' >&2; exit 1
fi
perl bench/matrix-check.pl bench/operation-matrix-select-current.json "$wump_evidence/matrix-current.json" > "$wump_evidence/matrix-check.txt"
wump_fresh=$?
perl bench/matrix-check.pl bench/operation-matrix-callee-baseline.json "$wump_evidence/matrix-current.json" > "$wump_evidence/matrix-anchor-check.txt"
wump_anchor=$?
printf 'Previous selection gate exit: %s; retained-anchor gate exit: %s\n' "$wump_fresh" "$wump_anchor"
if [ "$wump_fresh" -ne 0 ] || [ "$wump_anchor" -ne 0 ]; then exit 1; fi

validation_note:
XS / JSON checkpoint, 2026-11-01 local date (final runs continue into Nov 2 UTC).

Source checkpoints: edf40ee isolates ordinary JSON::PP reentrant call state;
8d78b10 admits guarded utf8::encode/decode and repairs module scratch,
publication/localization markers, namespace/class metadata and TEMP writes;
9638d8c rejects reuse of published debugger arguments; aeb86f6 makes that
regression wait for explicit worker completion; 4365dac fixes incremental
runtime-object dependencies. Runtime C behavior itself is unchanged here.

Normal full project checks pass at the final caller-guard source. Parser
regeneration passes with Bison 3.8.2. Before the last caller guard, the full
upstream harness passes 2,919 files / 1,351,311 checks in 391 seconds, TZ=UTC,
at source 8d78b10. After that guard, all upstream Carp/JSON::PP tests plus
porting diagnostics/customization pass: 84 files / 28,508 checks in 90 seconds.
No full upstream rerun after the guard is claimed. Default upstream skips
remain visible; no tests or expected values were changed to force a pass.

The full ASan project suite passes at 8d78b10. LSan with full teardown passes
miniperl and utf8-xs(16), json-state(11), json-parallel(18),
element-mark-parallel(4), gv-parallel(4), caller-parallel(8 before the final
guard), and native-select(133). After the final guard and corrected relink,
LSan again passes caller-parallel(12), json-parallel(18), and utf8-xs(16).

Whole-core scoped TSan passes utf8-xs, JSON, caller/Carp, element publication,
namespace/class queries, native-select and parallel; rebuilt module checks
also pass encode-parallel(10), bytes-parallel(6), xs-parallel(68), and
native-integration(12). After the final guard and corrected relink, the
caller(12), JSON(18) and allocator fixtures pass again. The deliberate
Perl_more_bodies race is detected. The existing full-project upstream
ithreads clone race remains open; no whole-upstream sanitizer pass is claimed.

Pre-fix controls demonstrate failures: the ordinary reentrant JSON suite fails
4/11 on the old binary; the parallel JSON suite fails 14/18; old TSan builds
expose marker and named-sort races. The new caller-reuse regression fails
4/12 before its guard. The incremental dependency regression fails 3/6 before
the rule change and passes all 6 afterward. All six runtime object members
are checked byte-for-byte against each final normal/ASan/TSan Perl archive.

Failed iterations remain in validation-logs. These include an initial
unnecessary Scalar::Util registration experiment (removed: Perl 5.42 uses
builtin aliases), a missing upstream diagnostic entry (fixed), exposed races,
and test-fixture mistakes corrected without dropping error cases. The last
incremental sanitizer command initially omitted runtime flags; correcting the
objects then exposed a stale archive dependency. Wrong-configuration TSan
failures and ASan missing-fiber warnings are retained. The dependency fix
forces a real relink, after which focused sanitizer checks pass without
suppressions or output filtering. Those failed iterations are not evidence
of a sanitizer pass or a new production-runtime defect.

Compatibility remains entry-specific. Unsupported UTF-8 magic/reference
inputs, other unadmitted XSUBs, runtime compilation/autoloading, general
debugger behavior, arbitrary native affinity and shared IO ownership remain
outside this checkpoint. Caller inspection must localize fresh scratch after
publishing an owning argument array; raw still-borrowed arrays cannot escape.

The final binary also passes fresh stock differentials: context-compat(53)
and legacy-compat(26). The final dependency/source checks pass as well.
The matrix completes all 770 observations (650 successful, versus the old
capture's 640); the new successes are JSON on two/four slots. Both +10% gates
fail exactly two metrics: one-slot JSON work/process is +21.48%/+21.41%
against selection and +18.73%/+18.67% against the retained anchor. Every other
previously supported metric passes. JSON work is 53.74/53.48/53.64 us on
one/two/four slots: admission works, but this fixture does not scale. No
primary fixture, baseline, failed sample or comparison budget was changed.

Additional final Mojolicious 9.37 integration: CLI(54), single-slot jobs(42),
and in-process service(66) pass. The prepared live server passes all 48
HTTP/WebSocket/shutdown/listener-reuse checks on each of one/four slots.
An attempted four-slot in-process jobs run is rejected by Test2/API.pm:72's
INIT-time string eval at the existing compiler gate. These in-process scripts
assert single-slot behavior and were not modified to force four-slot passes.
That failure is retained separately from the passing external-client live
server coverage. No general Test2-in-parallel or runtime compilation support
is claimed.
